Data behind the difference map

Source: R/plot.R
plot_data.Rd

Returns the exact table plot_diff() draws, without requiring ggplot2. This makes row ordering, binning, and the match classification of every tile visible and testable.

plot_data(cmp, columns = NULL, max_rows = 500L, row_bins = 100L)

Arguments

cmp

A daffiz_comparison from compare_dt().

columns

Optional character vector of compared measures to include. Defaults to every compared measure, in input-column order.

max_rows

Largest number of records drawn one tile per row. Above this, rows are binned. NULL or Inf never bins.

row_bins

Maximum number of row bins used when binning applies.

Value

A data.table with one row per tile.

Details

There is one record per tile. Rows appear in original source position order, never ranked, so that regressions concentrated in one region of the input remain visible as a band. When the comparison has more than max_rows aligned or side-only records, contiguous rows are aggregated into at most row_bins bins and binned is TRUE; every eligible row is represented either way, and no row is ever discarded.

fraction_mismatched is the share of cells behind the tile that are not equal. Unbinned tiles cover one cell, so it is 0 or 1 there, and match_type, symbol and the source values are populated. Binned tiles cover several cells, so those per-cell columns are NA. row_start and row_end give the tile's extent in display order either way.

Examples

x <- data.frame(id = 1:3, amount = c(10, 20, 30))
y <- data.frame(id = 1:3, amount = c(10, 25, 27))
cmp <- compare_dt(x, y)
plot_data(cmp)
#>    row_rank row_label row_start row_end .row_x .row_y column match_type symbol
#>       <int>    <char>     <int>   <int>  <int>  <int> <char>     <fctr> <char>
#> 1:        1 x:1 / y:1         1       1      1      1 amount      equal       
#> 2:        2 x:2 / y:2         2       2      2      2 amount       diff      !
#> 3:        3 x:3 / y:3         3       3      3      3 amount       diff      !
#>    matched n_cells n_mismatched fraction_mismatched value_x value_y  diff
#>     <lgcl>   <int>        <int>               <num>   <num>   <num> <num>
#> 1:    TRUE       1            0                   0      10      10     0
#> 2:   FALSE       1            1                   1      20      25    -5
#> 3:   FALSE       1            1                   1      30      27     3
#>    abs_diff binned n_rows n_rows_total n_rows_shown
#>       <num> <lgcl>  <int>        <int>        <int>
#> 1:        0  FALSE      1            3            3
#> 2:        5  FALSE      1            3            3
#> 3:        3  FALSE      1            3            3
